generated.title: NEW YORK WIPED OUT BY A TSUNAMI?! 🌊 #shorts
generated.description:
Could a monster tsunami really wipe out New York City?

The Atlantic has produced deadly tsunamis before. In 1929, a magnitude 7.2 earthquake struck off Newfoundland and triggered a massive underwater landslide. The tsunami killed 28 people, and its waves were recorded on tide gauges as far south as Charleston, South Carolina.

So could a tsunami reach New York? Yes. NOAA and USGS rate the U.S. Atlantic coast's tsunami hazard as very low to low, but not zero.

And the famous mega-tsunami theory about a collapsing volcano on La Palma in the Canary Islands? USGS scientists say that nightmare scenario doesn't hold up: volcanic flank collapses tend to happen piecemeal, not in one giant slide.

Myth or fact? The threat is real. The Hollywood disaster is not.

Official tsunami alerts:
https://www.tsunami.gov/

This educational video includes AI-generated illustrations of a hypothetical scenario and schematic scientific visualizations. They are not real footage, documented tsunami imagery or predictions of future flooding.
